intent.title: the engine issue-recovery journal was deleted and silently re-initialized, and its activation lives nowhere durable
intent.what_this_is:
The durable recovery journal that every engine-authored issue is written through (the `codex/engine-issue-recovery` branch, pinned by the operator-owned activation file) no longer descends from the genesis the operator activated. The runbook's rule is that missing or corrupt journal state requires restoration and never initialization over the old record; that rule was crossed, and nothing in the machinery caught it.

- **Timeline (GitHub events and session logs, all under the operator's account):** 2026-09-12 04:12Z a Codex session activated the journal at genesis `f0e8c31a0d9d` and filed #1298 and #1299 through it (last old tip `1df92b85b2aa`, 04:14Z). 2026-09-12 05:02Z the branch was deleted; no session log or memory record names the actor. 2026-09-13 17:57Z a Claude session in a Build worktree was refused with "Recovery setup required", followed the message literally, ran `recovery init --confirm`, which succeeded because the ref was absent, created a fresh journal at genesis `aa42f2c8727a`, filed #1306, and then moved the untracked activation file out of its worktree into its session scratchpad.
- **Result:** two journal lineages exist. The old one (records for #1298, #1299, both confirmed) is unreachable from the branch and is preserved only because this session created `archive/engine-issue-recovery-2026-09-12-genesis-f0e8c31a` pointing at its last tip. The live one holds only #1306's record. The only activation file that matched the live branch sat in a scratchpad; the one in a Codex worktree from 2026-09-11 still pins the deleted genesis and now refuses every filing with "recovery journal genesis is missing from history".
- **Three defects, not one:** (1) `recovery init` cannot tell a never-activated repository from a deleted journal, so a session following the refusal text re-initializes over lost history; the runbook forbids exactly that but only in prose. (2) The activation file is untracked in every checkout, so a Build session treats it as clutter and moves it out, and no checkout can file an engine issue without re-deriving it. The runbook says it should be reviewed through the normal PR process and preserved across upgrades; today it is not. (3) Nothing detects or alarms on the journal branch being deleted, so a 25-hour gap passed unnoticed until the next filing.
- **What this session did to unblock filing:** pinned the live genesis `aa42f2c8727a` in this worktree with the sanctioned `recovery init --genesis --repository-id --confirm` restore (which verified the live chain), and filed this issue and one other through it. That ratifies the new lineage locally only; it did not touch the branch or the old lineage.
intent.whats_next:
Two operator decisions and one code fix.

- **Decide the authoritative lineage.** Keep the live journal (genesis `aa42f2c8727a`): nothing of value is lost because every old record was already confirmed-created, and the archive branch keeps the old lineage inspectable. Or restore the old lineage by re-pointing the branch to `1df92b85b2aa`, which is a forced ref update that discards #1306's record and the 2026-09-13 activation. Keeping the live journal is the recommended path.
- **Make the activation durable.** Land `.engine/operator-issue-recovery.json` for the chosen genesis through a PR as the runbook already intends, so every checkout can file and no session mistakes it for clutter. If it must stay out of upstream contributions, the erasure list is the place to say so, not an untracked file.
- **Fix the machinery so this cannot recur silently.** `recovery init` refuses when an activation exists locally or a journal commit for this repository can be found, and names the restore command instead; the refusal text for a missing activation stops pointing at plain `init --confirm` when a journal has ever existed. Add a health detector that alarms when the pinned genesis is not an ancestor of the journal branch, or the branch is absent. Consider moving the ref out of the `codex/` namespace so branch cleanups cannot sweep it. Release impact is patch: it tightens existing recovery behavior and adds no capability.

intent.title: A scoped repair round assessed after a refreshed deliverable review is anchored before that review, so it exempts nothing
intent.what_this_is:
The build coordinator measures each repair round from the previous repair round's final commit (`_classification_anchor`). When a fresh five-lens deliverable review is run in between (a new deliverable packet on a later commit), the next scoped repair round is still anchored at the OLD round's final commit, which predates the refreshed review's tip. The deliverable-coverage rule (`_coverage_result.apply_scope`) only lets a scoped round exempt the lenses it did not name when the round's anchor sits at or after an original deliverable tip (`after_original`), so that round's exemption is silently discarded: the lenses the session deliberately left out are charged the whole fix as unread, and `status` demands their receipts as if no judgment had been made.

- Observed on the C4 write-authority Build (pull request 1257): round 5 was a fresh five-lens deliverable review at 84e63ef6; the round-5 fix (3e834da1) was judged `scoped` with the divergence-hunter lens only, but the round was anchored at 46305cab (round 3's final commit), and the other four lenses were then reported as owing 3e834da1. A later scoped round anchored at 27541682 (after the refreshed tip) exempted its range correctly, which is what isolates the anchor as the cause.
- The session cannot repair this itself: `none` needs the deliverable scope complete (circular), and a multi-lens scoped round is counted and stops at the escalation budget for a read the coordinator already excused.
intent.whats_next:
Decide where the anchor should move: when the deliverable review has been refreshed since the previous repair round, the next round's anchor should be the refreshed review's reviewed commit (the newest of the previous round's final commit and the deliverable tip), and `after_original` should then admit it. A regression test: a repair round, a deliverable re-packet on a later commit, then a scoped round naming one lens; the other lenses must be exempt from that round's range.

- Until then, a Build in this shape needs either a counted multi-lens re-read (operator guidance at the escalation budget) or an operator decision to accept the coverage gap as disclosed.

Program orchestration runbook (the generated file at rest)

intent.title: generated PROGRAM.md repeats every replaced objective in full, so program files grow to hundreds of kilobytes
intent.what_this_is:
The generated program file (PROGRAM.md, rendered by the Program Manager from each program's record) has become unreadable for the largest programs, and the cause is how revision history is rendered, not how much the programs contain.

- **What it is:** the projection's "How the objective has been revised" section prints the complete text of every replaced objective (`Previously: …`), and the intended-order history prints every replaced intent statement in full. A program whose objective is 10-15 KB and has been revised nine or ten times carries nine or ten full copies of that prose.
- **Measured on the current plan library (2026-09-13):** Deterministic Engine runtime with SQLite is 503 KB, of which 421 KB is replaced-objective text (9 copies) and 52 KB is intended-order history. Evidence-backed Engine Knowledge is 471 KB (350 KB replaced objectives, 75 KB intended-order history). Supervised implementation with specialized workers is 421 KB (392 KB replaced objectives). Assignment-scoped permission broker is 167 KB (132 KB replaced objectives). The current objective in each case is 5-15 KB.
- **Why it matters:** the generated file is the program's reading surface for the operator and for sessions. At these sizes no session can read one whole, so the current contract at the top is buried under history, and the portfolio's own plan collection feels unmanageable when the live content is small. Every revise-objective call makes it worse.
- **Where the rendering lives:** `.engine/tools/plan_program.py`, the projection's objective-history loop (`Previously: {entry['objective']}`) and the intended-order history rendering (`Previously: {prior['title']} — {prior['statement']}`). The record itself (`record.json`) rightly keeps full history; the defect is that the projection replays all of it inline.
intent.whats_next:
A small change in the projection, not in the record: keep the full history in the record and render it compactly.

- Render each replaced objective as its timestamp, reason and a short excerpt (for example the first line or a bounded number of characters), with the full prior text available on demand (a `program show --history` view, or a separate generated history file beside PROGRAM.md).
- Apply the same bound to the intended-order history's `Previously` lines.
- Keep the current objective and current intended order rendered in full; they are the contract.
- Add a test that a program with several long replaced objectives renders a PROGRAM.md whose size is bounded by its current content, not by its revision count.
- Run `program reproject` after the fix so the existing generated files converge.

No operator decision is needed beyond scheduling the fix. The release impact is patch: it corrects a generated view and changes no record, verb, or contract.

**What this is.** The #1307 fix (issue #1306) chooses the anchor for a scoped repair round correctly from now on, but the coverage rule reads the anchor STORED on each recorded round, so a round recorded before the fix keeps its wrong anchor and its exemption stays discarded. A Build that hit #1306 before the fix landed is not repaired by merging the fix.

The new `carried_tips` admission does not apply either: the four lenses' receipts ARE the refreshed-identity reads at 84e63ef6, so they are skipped, and the divergence-hunter receipt is under a different packet identity.
- No coordinator verb re-anchors a recorded round: `reconcile` needs a history rewrite, `none` needs the deliverable scope complete (circular), a multi-lens scoped round is counted and this Build is past the round ceiling, and editing snapshot.json by hand is forbidden.
